### athyg-replacement-strategy
Before designing or filing anything touching catalogue membership, star naming, identifier cross-matching, or per-field value sourcing: read docs/catalog-driver.md first.

AT-HYG is not a source. The durable contract, the strict residual policy (spine printed cells, *_src=OTHER, ledgered record drops and the spineDropped zero-pins) and the second-order role of SIMBAD all live in that doc, in more detail than any summary here.

Work tracking and the audit empirics: epic stellata-3bsf, then stellata-cns, then stellata-3f8, dependency-linked in that order.

### omp-s-documentation-read-it-from-the-source
omp's documentation: read it from the source repo, not the website. https://omp.sh/docs is a client-rendered single-page app — WebFetch gets 403 and curl gets an empty shell. The real docs are markdown in github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi under docs/ (public): shallow sparse clone the docs folder. Check the repo HEAD date against the installed 'omp --version' before trusting it.

The pages that matter for harness integration: extension-loading.md (discovery roots and the factory contract), extensions.md (the full event surface), hooks.md, compaction.md, session.md, tools/*.md (one per tool, with the real input schemas), task-agent-discovery.md.

The binary also carries its docs, but compressed — 'strings' finds only the filename index, and 'omp docs' opens a TUI that prints nothing when piped.

### stellata-bug-sweep-handoff
At the end of any bug-fix session in stellata where queued bugs remain, produce
a handoff prompt to paste into the next /clear'd session — unasked, as a code
block so it copy-pastes cleanly. Don't produce one when the queue is exhausted.

Why: /clear between bugs, then bootstrap the next session from a self-contained
prompt rather than re-deriving state.

The six-part format (open PRs awaiting smoke, remaining bugs in priority order,
skipping list, per-bug workflow reminder) is in docs/bd-workflow.md
§ Bug-sweep handoff.

### stellata-smoke-tests
# UI smoke tests — manual only, no dev server

UI changes get verified manually in the browser. Do NOT start a dev server
(`npm run dev`) — one is always already running, and an extra process competes
for ports. Do NOT write throwaway smoke scripts (Python / Node / Playwright):
the WebGL render loop holds the GPU and headless screenshots stall on
ReadPixels readback.

How to apply: after UI / shader / renderer changes, run typecheck + vitest,
then specify exactly what to look at in the browser — named stars to focus,
magnitude slider values, mode transitions, debug HUDs. Be specific.

DOM-only smoke scripts work for wiring bugs (no GPU readback), but use them
only when explicitly asked.

### task-tracking-policy
Overrides the bd prime Core Rule that prohibits TodoWrite and TaskCreate. That built-in is too strict; this split is the actual policy.

- Beads is canonical for anything that should outlive the session: tasks, bugs, refactors, follow-ups, design decisions. File the bead BEFORE writing code, mark in_progress when starting, close when shipped.
- TaskCreate is allowed for in-session step decomposition: sub-steps of an in-flight bead too granular to file individually and with no value next session.
- Never markdown TODO files. They decay silently and are not searchable.

How to apply: default to filing a bead, since persistence you do not need beats lost context. Single-step changes need neither. If a sub-step grows into its own commit or cross-session work, lift it to a bead and drop the task entry.

### worktree-public-artifact-symlinks
Never symlink public/ build artifacts from the main checkout into a worktree.

# The trap

A fresh worktree has no public/ artifacts (gitignored), so artifact-backed
suites self-skip. Symlinking them in from the main checkout makes the tests run
— and then any build in that worktree writes THROUGH the symlinks into the MAIN
checkout's public/, leaving a main checkout whose artifacts disagree with each
other. That silent mismatch is exactly what tests/artifact-freshness.test.ts
exists to catch.

# How to apply

- Need artifacts in a worktree for a read-only test run? COPY them (`cp`), or
  symlink and then materialise (`rm link && cp target link`) before ANY build.
- Before running build:catalog / build:binaries-runtime in a worktree, confirm
  nothing under public/ is a symlink: `find public -maxdepth 1 -type l`.
- Repairing a clobber: rebuild in the affected checkout, forcing past the mtime
  gate — `rm -f public/catalog-manifest.json` first, or `UPDATE_BUILD_COUNTS=1`.
- mtime side effect: a fresh worktree's LFS checkout of
  data/binaries/multiples.tsv is NEWER than a symlinked binaries.bin, which
  fails artifact-freshness until the mtimes are aligned (`touch -r`).

See [[stellata-smoke-tests]] for the no-dev-server rule that pairs with this.


# 🚨 SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL 🚨

**CRITICAL**: Before saying "done" or "complete", you MUST run this checklist:

```
[ ] bd close <id1> <id2> ...   (close completed issues)
```



## Core Rules
- **Default**: Use beads for ALL task tracking (`bd create`, `bd ready`, `bd close`)
- **Prohibited**: Do NOT use TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown files for task tracking
- **Workflow**: Create beads issue BEFORE writing code, mark in_progress when starting
- **Memory**: Use `bd remember "insight"` for persistent knowledge across sessions. Do NOT use MEMORY.md files — they fragment across accounts. Search with `bd memories <keyword>`.
- Persistence you don't need beats lost context
- Git authority: no git operations in this context
- Git workflow: stealth mode (no git ops)
- Session management: check `bd ready` for available work

## Essential Commands

### Finding Work
- `bd ready` - Show issues ready to work (no blockers)
- `bd list --status=open` - All open issues
- `bd list --status=in_progress` - Your active work
- `bd show <id>` - Detailed issue view with dependencies

### Creating & Updating
- `bd create --title="Summary of this issue" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task|bug|feature --priority=2` - New issue
  - Priority: 0-4 or P0-P4 (0=critical, 2=medium, 4=backlog). NOT "high"/"medium"/"low"
- `bd create ... --parent=<id>` - Hierarchical child (task under epic, subtask under task; inherits parent labels)
- `bd update <id> --claim` - Claim work
- `bd update <id> --assignee=username` - Assign to someone
- `bd update <id> --title/--description/--notes/--design` - Update fields inline
- `bd close <id>` - Mark complete
- `bd close <id1> <id2> ...` - Close multiple issues at once (more efficient)
- `bd close <id> --reason="explanation"` - Close with reason
- **Tip**: When creating multiple issues/tasks/epics, use parallel subagents for efficiency
- **WARNING**: Do NOT use `bd edit` - it opens $EDITOR (vim/nano) which blocks agents

### Dependencies & Blocking
- `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>` - Add dependency (issue depends on depends-on)
- `bd blocked` - Show all blocked issues
- `bd show <id>` - See what's blocking/blocked by this issue

### Sync & Collaboration
- `bd search <query>` - Search issues by keyword

### Project Health
- `bd stats` - Project statistics (open/closed/blocked counts)
- `bd doctor` - Check for issues (sync problems, missing hooks)
- `bd doctor --check=conventions` - Check for convention drift (lint, stale, orphans)

### Quality Tools
- `bd create --validate` - Check description has required sections
- `bd create --acceptance="criteria"` - Set acceptance criteria (checked by --validate)
- `bd create --design="decisions"` - Record design decisions
- `bd create --notes="context"` - Add supplementary notes
- `bd config set validation.on-create warn` - Auto-validate on every create
- `bd lint` - Check existing issues for missing sections

### Lifecycle & Hygiene
- `bd defer <id> --until="date"` - Defer work to a future date
- `bd supersede <id> --with=<new-id>` - Mark issue as superseded
- `bd close <id> --suggest-next` - Show newly unblocked issues after closing
- `bd stale` - Find issues with no recent activity
- `bd orphans` - Find issues with broken dependencies
- `bd preflight` - Pre-PR checks (lint, stale, orphans)
- `bd human <id>` - Flag for human decision (list/respond/dismiss)

### Structured Workflows
- `bd formula list` - See available workflow templates
- `bd mol pour <name>` - Start structured workflow from formula

## Common Workflows

**Starting work:**
```bash
bd ready           # Find available work
bd show <id>       # Review issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim it
```

**Completing work:**
```bash
bd close <id1> <id2> ...    # Close all completed issues at once
```

**Creating dependent work:**
```bash
# Run bd create commands in parallel (use subagents for many items)
bd create --title="Implement feature X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=feature
bd create --title="Write tests for X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task
bd dep add beads-yyy beads-xxx  # Tests depend on Feature (Feature blocks tests)
```
